Implement the redesigned dashboard nav/shell as REAL code in /opt/nxeon-sandbox (an isolated sandbox clone of the Nxeon platform — do NOT touch /opt/nxeon or /opt/nxeon-staging). This app is LIVE-SERVING right now via systemd (`nxeon-sandbox-web`/`nxeon-sandbox-worker`) at https://flow.k9x4rq7wpz2ah6t.nxeon.cloud — running `npm run build` in place while it's live briefly breaks asset serving for anyone hitting it mid-build (a previous agent's build did exactly this and had to be fixed with a restart). So: verify your work with `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` only. Do NOT run `npm run build` and do NOT restart/touch the systemd services — someone else will do one coordinated final build+restart once all parallel work lands.

## What already exists (a foundation agent just finished this — read, don't recreate)
- `/opt/nxeon-sandbox/components/portal-v2/icons.tsx` — ~30 hand-drawn 24×24 stroke icon components (e.g. `IconOverview`, `IconServers`, `IconWallet`, `IconShieldCheck`, etc.) pulled from the approved shell mockup.
- `/opt/nxeon-sandbox/components/portal-v2/Stepper.tsx` — not relevant to you (wizard-only).
- `/opt/nxeon-sandbox/components/portal-v2/primitives.tsx` — `Surface`, `IconTile`, `Pill`, `StatusPill`, `StatCardV2`, `Gauge`, `BarMeter`.
- `/opt/nxeon-sandbox/app/globals.css` — new additive `@theme` tokens: `--color-pv-bg/-surface-1/-surface-2/-text/-text-muted/-text-faint/-brand/-brand-light/-cyan/-blue/-good/-warn/-bad` (→ `bg-pv-*`/`text-pv-*`/`border-pv-*` utilities), `--radius-pv-sm/md/lg/xl` (→ `rounded-pv-*`), `--font-pv-display`/`--font-pv-body` (Sora/Inter, → `font-pv-display`/`font-pv-body`), plus `@layer components` classes `.pv-surface`, `.pv-surface-elevated`, `.pv-ambient` (the ambient gradient-blob background, pure CSS, respects `prefers-reduced-motion`), `.pv-nav-item` / `.pv-nav-item-active` (the floating-glow active nav pill — built exactly for what you're about to do).
- `/opt/nxeon-sandbox/app/layout.tsx` already loads Sora+Inter via `next/font/google` (CSS vars `--font-portal-sora`/`--font-portal-inter`) — the OLD Geist-based `font-sans` default is UNCHANGED for the ~54 pages not being redesigned.

## Read these before writing any code
1. `/tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/portal-redesign-shell.html` — the approved mockup for exactly this: new intent-based nav (Overview/Infrastructure/Grow/Build/Account groups), floating-glow active-nav-item, ambient gradient-blob hero, new stat-card/activity-feed/quick-actions layout.
2. `/root/.claude/plans/validated-napping-possum.md` — ground truth: current nav lives in `app/dashboard/layout.tsx:33-96` (`NavSection[]`, 7 groups, hand-rolled inline SVG icons via `Icon()` in `components/portal/Shell.tsx:182`).
3. Read the CURRENT `app/dashboard/layout.tsx` and `components/portal/Shell.tsx` in full to understand exactly what real data/props/auth/role-gating logic (`canAccess`, admin-only items, badges like the support "awaiting" counter) currently flows into the nav — your new nav must preserve ALL of this real functionality (every real destination, every role gate, every live badge count), just presented in the new visual language and new grouping. Do not drop or fake any of it.

## What to build
1. A new dashboard shell component (e.g. `components/portal-v2/DashboardShellV2.tsx`) implementing the shell mockup's structure: intent-based nav groups (Overview / Infrastructure / Grow / Build / Account — map every CURRENT real nav item into whichever new group makes sense; use your judgment matching the mockup's grouping logic, but don't invent destinations that don't exist and don't drop any that do), the floating-glow active-item treatment (`.pv-nav-item-active`), the new icon set from `icons.tsx` (map each current inline-SVG icon to its closest new equivalent; where the mockup already defined a specific icon for a nav concept, use that one).
2. Wire it into `app/dashboard/layout.tsx` so it actually renders for real dashboard traffic — replacing the current `Shell`/nav usage. This is the single highest-leverage file: getting this right makes the whole redesign real and clickable; done wrong, it silently breaks navigation for the entire portal.
3. A redesigned `/dashboard` overview page (or update the existing one) using `.pv-ambient` for the ambient background and `StatCardV2`/`Surface` from primitives for the stat-card/activity-feed/quick-actions layout shown in the mockup — using REAL data already fetched by the current `app/dashboard/page.tsx` (server balance, server count, recent activity, etc. — read that file first, keep its real data-fetching, just restyle the render).

## Constraints
- This sandbox has a real demo customer account (`you@nxeon.local`) with a running demo VPS, a running demo Minecraft server, an active demo domain, and an active demo hosting account — your nav and overview page will be exercised against this REAL data, not empty/mock state, so make sure it renders correctly for an account that actually has stuff in it.
- Preserve every real auth/role gate exactly (don't show admin-only items to non-admins, keep the support-ticket "awaiting" badge logic if it exists, etc.).
- Keep mobile responsive behavior working — check the mockup and the current `Shell.tsx` for how the sidebar collapses on small screens and replicate that interaction in the new version.
- No new external dependencies (no icon library, no CSS framework beyond Tailwind v4 already in use).

## When done
Report: exact files created/modified, confirmation `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` passes cleanly, and a plain-English list of every real nav destination and which new group you placed it in (so a reviewer can spot anything dropped or misplaced).

1	# Nxeon customer portal redesign — mockups first, then an isolated sandbox
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	The customer portal (58 top-level sections under `app/dashboard`) grew feature-by-feature with no overall IA/flow planning — confirmed directly in the code: nav-array comments describe reactive merges ("Billing absorbed Invoices," "Refer & earn + Affiliate merged"), and `app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx` is 944 lines of stacked sections with no tabs, the clearest single example of organic bolt-on growth. The user wants a genuine ground-up redesign — new visual system (not a reskin of the current CSS/components), new custom icons, better-planned flows, real buyer-psychology attention on conversion-critical screens — but wants to see and approve mockups before any real code changes happen. Once approved, the design gets implemented for real in a fully isolated sandbox environment (own app/DB/subdomain, zero shared state with production or staging) where the whole purchase experience — paying, deploying a server, buying a domain — can be clicked through with fake money and nothing ever actually provisions, so the team can pressure-test flows safely before touching the real product.
6	
7	This plan has two phases with a hard approval gate between them: **Phase 1 (mockups) happens now, in this workspace, touching zero real code.** **Phase 2 (real isolated implementation) only starts once the user has explicitly approved the Phase 1 direction.**
8	
9	## Ground truth confirmed this session (not assumptions)
10	
11	- Nav lives in `app/dashboard/layout.tsx:33-96` (`NavSection[]`, 7 groups) with icons drawn as hand-rolled inline SVG keyed by string name via `Icon()` in `components/portal/Shell.tsx:182` — **no icon library exists anywhere in the codebase**, which is good news: custom icons continue an existing convention, not a foreign one.
12	- Brand tokens are real and dashboard-specific, defined via Tailwind v4 `@theme` custom properties in `app/globals.css`: `--color-brand-50…900` (violet, `#6f47f5` at 500), `--color-navy-950…600`, `--color-accent-blue` (`#3b82f6`), `--color-accent-cyan` (`#22d3ee`). These hues are the one thing that must carry through unchanged into the new visual system.
13	- Shared dashboard components: `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (PageHeader/StatCard/Badge/EmptyState), `components/ui/charts.tsx` (hand-rolled, dependency-free SVG charts — `ROADMAP.md:17` explicitly says don't add a chart library), `components/portal/PortalHero.tsx` (per-page header banner). `app/dashboard/settings/page.tsx` already uses a working `?tab=` server-rendered tab pattern worth extending elsewhere.
14	- The step-indicator component is duplicated **six different ways**: local `Stepper` functions in `DeployWizard.tsx:145`, `HostingDeployWizard.tsx`, `GameDeployWizard.tsx`, `DomainRegisterWizard.tsx`, plus hand-rolled different markup in `DomainTransferInWizard.tsx` and `MigrationWizard.tsx`.
15	- Trust/conversion components (`WizardReassuranceCard.tsx`, `PaymentTrustBar.tsx`, `WizardStickyCart.tsx`) carry **hard-won, explicitly documented honesty rules** — a money-back-guarantee claim was investigated and deliberately removed at least three times because no such policy is actually published. There are currently zero fabricated testimonials/countdowns/scarcity claims anywhere. Any new buyer-psychology work must stay within this discipline: better visual treatment of what's real, never invented claims.
16	- Sandbox infra is more built than expected: `lib/sandbox.ts`'s `SANDBOX` flag already inertly gates ~20 real-infra branches in `worker/index.ts` (confirmed lines 448, 627, 652-653, 670, 716, 809, 862, 881, 885, 911, 916, 972, 1028, 1034, 1043-1044, 1155, 1235, 1298, 1361, 1445, 1549, 1876, 1934) — Proxmox, OVH, Cloudflare DNS, SSH, cPanel are all already inert under it. **Two real gaps confirmed by direct grep**: `lib/actions.ts`'s `payAndDeploy` (~lines 516-612) has zero SANDBOX references anywhere near its Stripe call — the only branching is on `cardCents`/`freePath`, meaning it hits the real (test-mode) Stripe API today whenever wallet balance doesn't fully cover the price. `lib/registrar.ts`'s `registerDomain` (line 244) is gated only by env-var presence (`registrarConfigured()`, line 9), not `SANDBOX`, meaning a live name.com API call is one missing env check away.
17	- A reusable template for a 4th subdomain already exists: `/etc/nginx/sites-available/nxeon-staging-admin` is a hand-maintained (not `configure-domains.sh`-generated) vhost proxying an obscure hostname to an existing backend on its own cert — `configure-domains.sh`/`/etc/nxeon/domains.env` only supports exactly 3 fixed hostnames (BASE/ADMIN/STAGING) and won't generalize to a 4th automatically.
18	- `lib/actions-sandbox.ts`'s `sandboxTopUp(cents)` already exists and is already SANDBOX-gated (self-serve $1-1000 wallet top-up, no Stripe) — the fake-balance mechanism Phase 2 needs is already built.
19	
20	## Phase 1 — Mockups (now, this workspace, zero real code changes)

## Summary

Implemented the redesigned dashboard shell/nav and overview page for real, in `/opt/nxeon-sandbox` only. No build was run, no systemd services touched.

**Files created:**
- `/opt/nxeon-sandbox/components/portal-v2/DashboardShellV2.tsx` — the new customer-portal shell. It's a deliberate fork of `components/portal/Shell.tsx` (not a shared component) that drops the admin-only code paths (per-group collapse, `tag="ops"` branch, AdminIndicators) since it's used only by `app/dashboard/layout.tsx`. The admin ops portal (`app/admin/layout.tsx`) is untouched and still imports the original `Shell`.

**Files modified:**
- `/opt/nxeon-sandbox/app/dashboard/layout.tsx` — regrouped the `nav` array into the mockup's 5 intent-based groups and swapped new icon-key strings in; swapped `<Shell>` for `<DashboardShellV2>`. All feature-flag gating (`FEATURE_HREF`/`flags`), the support-ticket "awaiting" badge logic, and every banner/tracker child (UnverifiedEmailBanner, AnnouncementBanner, PurchaseTracker, SignupTracker, PartnerSourceCapture, HeardAboutUsPrompt, AnnouncementPopup) are untouched.
- `/opt/nxeon-sandbox/app/dashboard/page.tsx` — restyled using `.pv-ambient` for the hero, `StatCardV2`/`Surface` from `portal-v2/primitives.tsx`, and the new icon set — the server/audit-log/transaction data fetching (including `renewalCharge`, tax context, dedicated-IP/extra-disk/backup pricing) is byte-identical to before, just re-rendered.

**Type check:** `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` is clean for everything I touched. A full run currently reports 10 errors, all confined to `components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx` — I confirmed via file mtimes that this file was modified by a different, concurrently-running agent (the wizard-redesign work) seconds after I finished, well after my own last edit, so it's an unrelated in-flight change, not something I introduced.

**Nav destinations — old group → new group (all 25 real items preserved, none dropped):**
- Overview: Dashboard
- Infrastructure: Deploy, Servers, Shared Hosting, Game Servers (FREE tag kept), Server Directory, Volumes, **Migration Center** (moved here from old "Tools")
- Grow: Domains, Website builder, Calendar (both moved here from old "Network"), SSL certificates, Inbox, Mailboxes (both from old "Mail"), Refer & earn, **Partner Program** (moved here from old "Account")
- Build: Build with AI, Matrix, **Free tools** (moved here from old "Tools")
- Account: Billing, Team, Support (badge preserved), Activity, Settings, **What's New** (moved here from old "Tools")

One intentional deviation from the mockup: I did not add the static "NEW" pill the mockup shows on Refer & earn, since nothing in the real data model marks it as new — adding it would be a fabricated badge.

Four nav icons have no equivalent in the new `icons.tsx` set (Migration Center, Inbox, Calendar, What's New); rather than inventing new glyphs, I reused the exact path data from the old `Shell.tsx` icons map for those four, redrawn at the new icon set's 1.8 stroke convention, defined locally in `DashboardShellV2.tsx`.

All other real behavior verified preserved by inspection: mobile off-canvas drawer (Escape-to-close, `inert` when hidden), desktop rail collapse persisted to `localStorage`, notifications dropdown with optimistic mark-read, live Mail-unread poll, live Matrix running/update poll and tag, impersonation banner + exit, CurrencySwitcher, the CUSTOMER-only "Refer & earn" topbar shortcut, CommandPalette, FeedbackWidget, VisitTracker, and the TerminalDock/Compose/Matrix providers mounted at shell level so in-portal navigation doesn't tear down live sessions.
